Ranks of the order statistics reported under each scenario

Source: R/weights.R
scenario_ranks.Rd

For \(n = 4Q+1\): S1 reports ranks \((1, 2Q+1, 4Q+1)\) (min, median, max), S2 ranks \((Q+1, 2Q+1, 3Q+1)\) (the quartiles), S3 all five (Luo 2018 sec. 2.2; McGrath 2023 scenario labels). For \(n = 20m+1\): S4 reports the quartiles with the 10th and 90th percentiles at ranks \(2m+1\) and \(18m+1\), that is \(p(n-1)+1\) for \(p = 0.1, 0.9\), and S5 adds the minimum and maximum (Balakrishnan 2022 sec. 3.1, Scenarios 5 and 7).

Usage

scenario_ranks(n, scenario = c("S3", "S1", "S2", "S4", "S5"))

Arguments

n

A single integer sample size at which every reported value is one order statistic under type 7: odd \(n \ge 3\) under S1, \(n = 4Q + 1\) with \(Q \ge 1\) under S2 and S3, and \(n = 20m + 1\) with \(m \ge 1\) under S4 and S5. Any other \(n\) is an error here, while the other functions of the package accept it.

scenario

Character. One of "S1" (min, median, max), "S2" (three quartiles), "S3" (all five). McGrath 2023 labels; note Wan 2014's C2/C3 are S3/S2 respectively. Also "S4" (the quartiles with the 10th and 90th percentiles) and "S5" (all five with the two percentiles), the names of Wu, Shi and Tong (2026) for Scenarios 5 and 7 of Balakrishnan et al. (2022); only the BLUE ("blue") is defined for these two.

Value

Integer vector of ranks, increasing.

Details

These are the sample sizes at which every reported value is a single order statistic under R's default quantile definition (type 7). At other sample sizes the functions of the package build the reported values from two adjacent order statistics each (see imputed_moments).

References

Wu Z, Shi J, Tong T (2026). Precision of the imputed mean and standard deviation from a five-number summary. Manuscript.

Examples

scenario_ranks(25, "S3")
#> [1]  1  7 13 19 25
